Yonhap NewsMinus 7.6%. That was the decline of the KOSPI index last week. After appearing set to reach "10,000-pi" (KOSPI 10,000) last month, the index turned lower, and a correction has now lasted nearly a month. Amid this, there was some welcome news. SK hynix's (000660.KS) American Depositary Receipts (ADRs) successfully listed and surged. In this week's Sunday Money Cafe, we revisit the week's market conditions and examine whether the SK hynix ADR listing could serve as a springboard for a rebound next week.A Rare "Pillar of Fire"… KOSPI and KOSDAQ Close Higher TogetherAccording to the Korea Exchange on the 12th, the KOSPI index closed at 7,475.94 on the 10th, up 2.52% from the previous trading day. The index jumped as much as 5.66% intraday, triggering a buy sidecar and briefly reclaiming the 7,700 level, but gave back a significant portion of its gains. The KOSDAQ index also triggered a buy sidecar and rebounded sharply by 5.47% to close at 837.43.The domestic stock market, which had been sluggish this week, appeared to regain upward momentum just before the weekend. Lee Kyoung-min, a researcher at Daishin Securities, analyzed that "the confirmation of solid investment demand for semiconductors supported investor sentiment and acted as upward pressure on the domestic stock market," while Kang Jin-hyuk, a researcher at Shinhan Investment & Securities, noted that "despite volatility in SK hynix shares, risk appetite recovered as noise in the AI (artificial intelligence) cycle subsided."There were also signs that the concentration in Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) and SK hynix was easing. By sector, defense and nuclear power theme stocks recorded steep rebounds, while gains in financial, securities, and insurance sectors—expected to benefit from the value-up program—as well as holding companies were also notable.However, unease persists. First, there are concerns about whether individual investors' "ammunition," which had supported the downside each time the market fell, has run out. According to the Korea Financial Investment Association, investor deposits stood at 107.1279 trillion won as of the 9th. This is the smallest amount since 104.1291 trillion won on February 20 this year. Investor deposits have declined for eight consecutive trading days since 132.4697 trillion won on the 29th of last month.The decline in deposits is interpreted as reflecting individual investors either engaging in bargain hunting or withdrawing funds altogether, after the KOSPI rose to an all-time closing high of 9,114.55 on the 22nd of last month, then plunged several times and at one point fell as low as 7,063.76 intraday. A decrease in investor deposits does not necessarily mean an exit from the market, but a reduction in standby funds can also be interpreted as a sign that the capacity to absorb selling by foreigners and others is weakening.The failure to hold onto intraday surges through the close is also a source of unease. On the 9th, the KOSPI soared as much as 4.1% intraday from the previous day's close, but gave back most of its gains to end up just 0.62%. On the 10th, even though a buy sidecar was triggered, it managed only a 2.52% gain. In other words, upward pressure is not strong.SK hynix's Successful Nasdaq DebutSK Group Chairman Chey Tae-won, SK hynix CEO Kwak Noh-jung, and SK hynix outside director and board chairman Koh Seung-beom, along with other executives and employees, mark the start of Nasdaq ADR trading at the "Opening Bell" event held at the Nasdaq MarketSite in New York, U.S. Yonhap NewsSK hynix, which entered Nasdaq through its ADR listing, made a successful debut on the 10th, its first trading day, surging more than 13%. SK hynix, which began trading at $170, at one point soared to $177 intraday, proving strong investor interest. However, it gave back some of its intraday gains to close its first day at $168.49. This is about 13.1% higher than the ADR offering price, which was set by reflecting an approximately 2.7% premium to SK hynix's three-day average share price on the Korea Exchange market.Converting the ADR closing price into won at the current exchange rate amounts to about 2.528 million won per Korean share. This is about 16% higher than SK hynix's regular-session closing price of 2.18 million won on the Korea Exchange on the 10th.
